ADJOURNED

  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES

  POLICY DEVELOPMENT SESSION

  MARCH 14, 2017

An adjourned meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to
order at 5:06 p.m. in the City Council Chambers, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, Rolling
Hills Estates, by MAYOR ZERUNYAN.

2.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present: Huff, Mitchell*, Schmitz, Zuckerman, Zerunyan
*COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL arrived at 5:08 p.m.

Staff Present:  City Manager Doug Prichard
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Assistant City Manager Greg Grammer
  Community Services Director Andy Clark
  Planning Director David Wahba
  Administrative Services Director Mike Whitehead
  Assistant to the City Manager Alexa Davis

3.  PUBLIC COMMENT

A.  Ron Uyeda, Peninsula resident, requested the COUNCIL to consider a Social Host
  Ordinance that addresses underage drinking parties with adult permission. He
  noted that this ordinance was adopted by the other three Peninsula cities and
  asked to have this item placed on the agenda.

  Heather Matson, Palos Verdes Peninsula Unified School District, also requested
  that the Social Host Ordinance be considered by the COUNCIL. She noted that
  social media has made it more difficult to control teenage parties.

  Andrea Vona, Executive Director, Palos Verdes Peninsula Land Conservancy,
  commented on the Conservancy’s partnership with the City. She asked the
  COUNCIL to consider a potential rehabilitation of the Nature Center buildings and
  urged the City to investigate long-term improvements.

  Ann Lampy, former PTA President, also asked the COUNCIL to consider adopting
  the Social Host Ordinance.

  Pam Schachter, 46 Ranchview Road, requested the COUNCIL to reconsider the
  off-street parking requirements for oversized vehicles. She further commented
  that something needs to be done to amend the Code as this is an ongoing problem
  the Ranchview neighborhood.

4.  ITEMS FOR DISCUSSION

A.  MID-YEAR REPORTS

  Recommendation: That the City Council receive and file these reports.

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL

  TO RECEIVE AND FILE THE MID-YEAR REPORTS.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZERUNYAN SO ORDERED.

ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES
POLICY DEVELOPMENT SESSION
MARCH 14, 2017
 B.  POLICY DEVELOPMENT SESSION ITEMS

  CITY MANAGER

  City Manager Contract Provisions – City Manager Prichard provided a staff report
  (as per agenda material).

  After brief discussion, MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF and COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL
  volunteered to serve on the subcommittee.

  Council/Staff Communications – City Manager Prichard provided a staff report (as
  per agenda material).

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL referred to a recent court decision regarding public
  information requests and suggested a meeting with the COUNCIL and City
  Attorney Davis. She noted that she serves on multiple boards and requested
  clarification on how to better manage these requests.

  City Attorney Davis responded that the City has been proactive in creating
  electronic media policies, but noted that the City’s email account should be
  utilized at all times.

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ also reminded everyone, when they are chairing
  committees, to make sure to communicate on the City’s email addresses.

  MAYOR ZERUNYAN noted his disappointment with the Supreme Court decision
  and believed their decision to be flawed. He further noted his opinion that
  legislation should be created in an effort to provide a better argument on the
  cities’ behalf.

  Training – Assistant to the City Manager Davis noted that there will be a social
  media training session on May 9, 2017 addressing the aforementioned issues.

  City Manager Prichard noted that harassment training and a Brown Act refresher
  will be provided by City Attorney Davis at a future meeting as well, and it would
  be helpful to know COUNCIL MEMBERS’ availability.

  Business License Ordinance Revisions – City Manager Prichard provided a staff
  report (as per agenda material). He noted that some of the provisions need to be
  clarified and an ordinance will be presented to the COUNCIL in the next few
  months. Additionally, City Attorney Davis noted that if tax amounts need to be
  adjusted, it must go before the voters.

  Salary Survey – City Manager Prichard provided a staff report (as per agenda
  material). He noted that any information gathered for the salary survey is for
  informational purposes only and the COUNCIL will still consider the ranges and
  rates through negotiations. He noted that it is reasonable to question the cost to
  conduct this survey, and that staff has contacted other firms to provide this
  service at a lesser cost than previously quoted.

  Following discussion, it was the consensus of the COUNCIL to have the Budget
  and Audit Committee work with staff on this issue.

  ASSISTANT CITY MANAGER/ASSISTANT TO THE CITY MANAGER

  CAPITAL PROJECTS BUDGET (ROADS, STORM DRAINS, CITY HALL):

  Street Maintenance – Assistant City Manager Grammer provided a staff report (as
  per agenda material). He noted that drainage improvements are needed along
  Palos Verdes Drive East as well as a long-range plan for curb, gutter, bike lanes,
  etc. He further noted that some of those improvements may not be undertaken at
  this time, but would look into obtaining grant funds to address the drainage
  issues and aesthetics.

ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
POLICY DEVELOPMENT SESSION
MARCH 14, 2017
   In response to COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ, Assistant City Manager Grammer
  noted that the long-range plan would take place over the next eight to 10 years.
  Planning Director Wahba then noted that Chadmar will undertake overlay of
  PVDE within the next year.

  Traffic Signal Pole Improvements – Assistant City Manager Grammer provided a
  staff report (as per agenda material).

  In response to COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ and COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN,
  Assistant City Manager Grammer noted that staff will look into the cost of repair
  rather than replacement.

  Storm Drain Inspection and Cleaning Update – Assistant City Manager Grammer
  provided a staff report (as per agenda material). He noted that the work should be
  completed in 35 days by Sancon Engineering.

  City Hall Upgrade – Assistant City Manager Grammer provided a staff report (as
  per agenda material).

  In response to COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN, Assistant City Manager Grammer
  stated that this project did not go out to bid and is on hold in an effort to see how
  the storm drain improvement costs pan out.

  Private Contractor for Public Works/Road Maintenance – Assistant City Manager
  Grammer provided a staff report (as per agenda material).

  After brief discussion, it was the consensus of the COUNCIL to direct staff to
  solicit proposals from private contractors.

  ADA Transition Plan – Assistant to the City Manager Davis provided a staff report
  (as per agenda material).

  After brief discussion, it was the consensus of the COUNCIL to proceed with the
  staff recommendation to allocate funds in the amount of $12,450 and enter into a
  Memorandum of Understanding with the CJPIA to be presented at a future
  COUNCIL meeting.

  PUBLIC SAFETY:

  Emergency Preparedness Coordinator – Assistant City Manager Grammer provided
  a staff report (as per agenda material).

  City Manager Prichard explained that to augment Area G, it may be appropriate to
  share emergency preparedness staff with the other Peninsula cities.

  It was the consensus of the COUNCIL to investigate this further.

  Parking Enforcement – Assistant City Manager Grammer provided a staff report (as
  per agenda material).

  Planning Director Wahba noted that the Sheriff’s Department has difficulty in
  consistently enforcing parking restrictions due to other commitments during
  patrol and response to calls for service.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL provided some history as to why overnight parking
  restrictions were put in place.

  COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN noted that he believes this enforcement helps the
  community by taking cars off the street.

  After brief discussion, it was the consensus of the COUNCIL to look into retaining
  a contractor to take over these duties.  Administrative Services Director
  Whitehead noted that the revenue generated by this practice could offset the cost.

ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
POLICY DEVELOPMENT SESSION
MARCH 14, 2017
   Social Host Ordinance – Assistant City Manager Grammer provided a staff report
  (as per agenda material).

  City Attorney Davis explained that this ordinance has been adopted by many
  cities and would be a useful tool.

  MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF noted that this should encourage parents who have
  teenagers to be more responsible.

  MAYOR ZERUNYAN suggested advertising this ordinance so that parents know
  what is expected. He then referred to the large party (more than 25 people)
  ordinance the City adopted years ago.

  Planning Director Wahba noted that a Temporary Use Permit is required for
  special events, i.e. weddings.

  City Manager Prichard noted that he will review the code for the large party
  ordinance, and if needed, bring back an ordinance addressing both issues.

  Traffic Control Contract Services – Assistant City Manager Grammer provided a
  staff report (as per agenda material).

  After brief discussion, it was the consensus of the COUNCIL to have staff review
  the various options available to continue managing traffic at Rancho Vista
  Elementary School since the Sheriff’s Traffic Control Deputy is retiring from that
  position.

  Neighborhood “Slow Down/Drive 25” Signs – Assistant City Manager Grammer
  provided a staff report (as per agenda material).

  MAYOR ZERUNYAN suggested obtaining more information from the City of
  Rancho Palos Verdes regarding this issue and perhaps remind residents on social
  media about slowing down in their neighborhoods.

  It was the consensus of the COUNCIL to follow this approach.

  Neighborhood Entryway Cameras – Assistant to the City Manager Davis provided
  a staff report (as per agenda material).

  Discussion ensued with City Manager Prichard noting that perhaps those
  intersections not covered by the ALPR cameras should be included.

  MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF referred to the Montecillo neighborhood where it was
  noted that the camera is located at the intersection of Palos Verdes Drive East and
  Palos Verdes Drive North and does not cover their entryway.

  MAYOR ZERUNYAN noted that the Dapplegray Homeowners’ Association
  purchased an ALPR camera for their entrance and is located on private property.
  Assistant to the City Manager Davis noted she will contact their HOA for further
  information.

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ noted that there are two issues; one with respect to
  those neighborhoods not currently covered by ALPR cameras and those
  neighborhoods who wish to obtain their own surveillance cameras.

  City Manager Prichard suggested identifying those intersections without ALPR
  coverage for possible camera installation and request the current contractor to
  perform an assessment of the cost of installation and bring back this item at the
  Budget Study Session.

  It was the consensus of the COUNCIL to follow this approach for City entries and
  provide individual neighborhoods who wish to obtain surveillance cameras with
  information, but no funding assistance.

ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
POLICY DEVELOPMENT SESSION
MARCH 14, 2017
   Drones – Assistant City Manager Grammer provided a staff report (as per agenda
  material).

  City Attorney Davis noted that the question is an enforcement issue.

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ commented that this is a problem in her
  neighborhood.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL suggested monitoring this and keeping track of how
  many complaints are received.

  It was the consensus of the COUNCIL to follow this approach.

  Coyote Management – Assistant to the City Manager Davis provided a staff report
  (as per agenda material).

  After some discussion, it was the consensus of the COUNCIL to continue
  monitoring this situation.

  PERSONNEL:

  Mission/Vision/Values – Assistant to the City Manager Davis provided a staff
  report (as per agenda material).

  Brief discussion ensued with City Manager Prichard noting that the idea is to
  create a mission statement internally with the staff participating in how they
  envision the City.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL and COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ volunteered to
  serve on the subcommittee.

  It was the consensus of the COUNCIL to follow this approach.

  PUBLIC INFORMATION:

  Newsletters – Assistant to the City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per
  agenda material).

  After some discussion, it was the consensus of the COUNCIL to continue utilizing
  electronic media to post the newsletters on the City’s website.

  Social Media/Community Outreach Update – Assistant to the City Manager Davis
  provided a staff report (as per agenda material).

  Brief discussion ensued regarding the features of the City’s newly updated
  website.

  Assistant to the City Manager Davis noted that the City’s Facebook page has been
  available for a year with the new website being boosted on that site.

  COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN inquired about the pictures shown on the website
  and asked if they could be modified to fit the page. Administrative Services
  Director Whitehead noted that the City’s website designer does not perform this
  function, but will look into this further.

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ suggested utilizing Instagram for various pictures.

  ***

  At 7:37 p.m., MAYOR ZERUNYAN called for a brief recess.

  ***

ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
POLICY DEVELOPMENT SESSION
MARCH 14, 2017
   ***
  At 7:45 p.m., the COUNCIL reconvened with MAYOR ZERUNYAN,
  MAYOR  PRO  TEM  HUFF,  COUNCILWOMAN  MITCHELL,
  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ, and COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN present.
  ***

  PLANNING DIRECTOR

  General Plan Update – Planning Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per
  agenda material). He noted that they have narrowed the firms down to two with
  the main differences being in price and completion date. He further noted his
  hope to retain a firm at the March 28 COUNCIL meeting and proceed in April or
  May.

  In response to COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL, COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ noted
  that the community will be completely engaged in this process.

  COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN believed this will be a good project for the entire
  community.

  Increase GIS Per-Parcel Fee – Planning Director Wahba provided a staff report (as
  per agenda material).

  It was the consensus of the COUNCIL to follow the staff recommendation to
  increase the radius map fee to $400 per parcel.

  Recreational Marijuana Regulations (Proposition 64) – Planning Director Wahba
  provided a staff report (as per agenda material).

  After some discussion, it was the consensus of the COUNCIL to direct staff to
  work with City Attorney Davis to develop regulations and amend the Municipal
  Code before the end of the year when the state regulations go into effect.

  Parking of Oversized Vehicles in Yard Areas Contiguous to the Street for Purposes of
  Loading and Unloading – Planning Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per
  agenda material).

  Extensive discussion ensued regarding residents who possess oversized vehicles
  and the normal routine they use when loading and unloading for a trip.

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ noted that it is not the intent of the City to penalize
  those residents who own these vehicles.

  MAYOR ZERUNYAN noted that these type of issues are really code enforcement
  and that to amend the code for one incident is not reasonable.

  It was the consensus of the COUNCIL to continue treating this matter as a code
  enforcement issue.

  Non-Permitted Grading in Rear Yards as it Relates to Drainage Issues – Planning
  Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per agenda material). He noted that
  this item will be presented to the COUNCIL at their next meeting.

  Extensive discussion ensued regarding whether or not to entertain the issue that
  the Dapplegray Homeowners’ Association brought up regarding backyard grading.

  COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN noted that the City’s Environmental Consultant
  Kathleen McGowan should also be informed of the progress on this project.

  In response to COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ, Planning Director Wahba stated that
  he informed the HOA that if the City were to undertake the repairs, an easement
  would be required and the residents were not in favor of that option.

ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  6
POLICY DEVELOPMENT SESSION
MARCH 14, 2017
   MAYOR ZERUNYAN noted that the major issue is June’s Trail which the City does
  intend to fund, but the City cannot pay for each individual property. He noted
  that the problems with the other trails are basically maintenance.

  Planning Director Wahba noted that he expects the plans for June’s Trail this
  week.

  It was the consensus of the COUNCIL to continue only with Transtech’s treatment
  of June’s Trail.

  Solar Photovoltaic Energy Systems for Residential Properties – This item was not
  discussed due to a pending public hearing.

  Community Choice Aggregation (CCA) – Planning Director Wahba provided a staff
  report (as per agenda material). He noted that a representative is tentatively
  scheduled to make a presentation at a future COUNCIL meeting.

  COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN noted that he has been involved with this committee
  and discussion focused primarily on the Joint Power Agreement. He noted his
  opinion that this was worth pursuing.

  It was the consensus of the COUNCIL to continue to be engaged in this process.

  UPDATE ON MAJOR PLANNING PROJECTS CITY-WIDE:

  Commercial District – Planning Director Wahba provided an update on the various
  projects noting that Orchard’s Supply is now open and a “chainsaw” cutting will
  take place on March 24. He noted that they are also interested in participating in
  the City’s Earth Day event.

  COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN suggested that Assistant City Manager Grammer
  and Community Services Director Clark set up purchase orders with Orchards.
  Community Services Director Clark responded that this is underway.

  Brickwalk – In response to COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN, Planning Director
  Wahba noted that the property owners have re-engaged their team in an effort to
  establish building pads. He further noted that the property owner is looking into
  options as to what they can build at that location.

  Planning Director Wahba noted that the property owners are working with Cotton-
  Shires to determine how best to provide stable buildings and that perhaps
  variances could be contemplated.

  City Attorney Davis cautioned that a forgiveness of fees would be considered as a
  subsidy.

  Cal Water Project – In response to MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF, Planning Director
  Wahba noted that this project should begin in 2018, but the actual start date is
  anticipated to be in April of that year. He noted that they are meeting with the
  School District on March 22.

  ADMINISTRATIVE SERVICES DIRECTOR

  Mid-Year Budget Review – Administrative Services Director Whitehead provided a
  staff report (as per agenda material).

  In response to COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN, Administrative Services Director
  Whitehead noted that the City is in a good position regarding the PERS obligation
  due to no safety personnel being involved He explained that he will have more
  information regarding those calculations at the Budget Study Session.

  City Manager Prichard noted that some of the development fees anticipated at the
  preparation of the budget have yet to be received due to delays in certain projects.

ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  7
POLICY DEVELOPMENT SESSION
MARCH 14, 2017
   He noted that when the fees are received, they will be booked into the appropriate
  fiscal year.

  Discussion ensued regarding the changes in PERS’ expected rates of return, and
  Administrative Services Director Whitehead indicated a thorough analysis will be
  presented at the Budget Study Session.

  Fiscal Health Report, FY 2005-06 through FY 2014-15 – Administrative Services
  Director Whitehead provided a staff report (as per agenda material).

  It was noted that all trends are either stable or positive.

  Finance Update – Administrative Services Director Whitehead provided a staff
  report (as per agenda material).

  FACILITY AND IT PROJECTS:

  City Hall Space Planning/Office Upgrades – Administrative Services Director
  Whitehead noted that this item has been deferred until the storm drain
  improvement costs are considered.

  Information Technology Projects – Administrative Services Director Whitehead
  provided a staff report (as per agenda material) and was pleased to note that the
  City now has state-of-the-art equipment.

  COMMUNITY SERVICES DEPARTMENT

  Senior Recreation Leader Position – Community Services Director Clark provided
  a staff report (as per agenda material).

  After some discussion, it was the consensus of the COUNCIL to consider
  allowing the Senior Recreation Leader to work up to 1,500 hours per year at an
  additional cost to the City of $1,351 along with required contributions to PERS.

  CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT PROJECTS:

  Palos Verdes Drive North Medians Landscaping Project – Community Services
  Director Clark provided a staff report (as per agenda material).

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL noted she was pleased with the appearance of the
  medians. City Manager Prichard noted that it is basic and asked if everyone
  liked the look.

  It was the consensus of the COUNCIL to move forward with landscaping the
  balance of the medians west of Hawthorne and on lower Silver Spur Road and
  authorize a budget adjustment as needed.

  Butcher Property Corner Development – Community Services Director Clark
  provided a staff report (as per agenda material).

  COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN suggested keeping this project as simple as
  possible. He cautioned the COUNCIL about setting high expectations for
  projects that might not occur.

  Nature Center – Community Services Director Clark provided a staff report (as
  per agenda material).

  MAYOR ZERUNYAN reported that he attended a meeting with the Palos Verdes
  Peninsula Land Conservancy, as well as other community representatives. He
  noted that they are looking for a permanent location. He further noted that
  discussion included the possibility of the City providing the land at
  PVDN/PVDE and the community representatives providing the development.

ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  8
POLICY DEVELOPMENT SESSION
MARCH 14, 2017
   City Manager Prichard suggested that a subcommittee be created to investigate
  this further.

  MAYOR ZERUNYAN and COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN volunteered to serve on
  this subcommittee.

  MAYOR ZERUNYAN then noted that he will contact Andrea Vona, Executive
  Director, PVPLC and set up a meeting to discuss this proposition.

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ noted to encourage LEED construction for any new
  buildings.

  City Hall Landscaping – Community Services Director Clark provided a staff
  report (as per agenda material).

  COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN commented that he would support taking this step
  because when summer comes, the landscaping will look tired.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL noted that if the City Hall is remodeled, it could
  damage some of the landscaping if trailers and containers are utilized.

  City Manager Prichard suggested taking a wait and see approach with the
  storm drain issues before moving on with the remodel project, which would
  have to be completed before any landscaping improvements take place.

  Ernie Howlett Park – Community Services Director Clark provided a staff report
  (as per agenda material).

  GRANTS STATUS:

  Peter Weber Equestrian Center Improvement Project – Community Services
  Director Clark provided a staff report (as per agenda material).

  City Manager Prichard noted that the City is still waiting for County
  reimbursement.

  Quimby Fees – Community Services Director Clark provided a staff report (as
  per agenda material).

  Chandler Contribution Fund – Community Services Director Clark provided a
  staff report (as per agenda material).

  COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN asked for an update on the boutique hotel
  discussion.

  Planning Director Wahba provided an update on the proposed boutique hotel
  that would replace the Norris Ballet Studio. He noted that he has been meeting
  with the hotel developers, and Jeff Axtell, Peninsula Center, and they have
  engaged an architect to look at the parking behind the gym. He further noted
  that they are meeting with the Norris Theater to consider relocation
  alternatives.

  MAYOR ZERUNYAN noted that he met with Dick Moe’s daughter, Julie, and
  that she acknowledged the hillside building would be a difficult undertaking.
  He further noted that he will meet with Mr. Axtell and reiterate the COUNCIL’S
  concerns with the current proposal. He then stated that Mr. Axtell agreed to
  assist the Norris Theater’s move to a smaller property and that office space
  would be needed as well.

  Miscellaneous

  City Manager Prichard noted the COUNCIL’S schedule in regards to attendance
  at upcoming meetings and that he will check with the various consultants’
  schedules for their presentations at future COUNCIL meetings.

ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  9
POLICY DEVELOPMENT SESSION
MARCH 14, 2017
 5.  ADJOURNMENT

  At 9:47 p.m., MAYOR ZERUNYAN formally adjourned the meeting.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Hope J. Nolan  Douglas R. Prichard
Deputy City Clerk  City Clerk

ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  10
POLICY DEVELOPMENT SESSION
MARCH 14, 2017
